newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police stop opposition crowd, tension high.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police stop opposition crowd, tension high.

text.p: Serbian security police halted 80,000 opposition protesters in downtown Belgrade on Monday in a dangerous new confrontation after bloody violence overnight in which more than 100 demonstrators were injured.

Police had allowed more than 20,000 student protesters to march over a Belgrade bridge two hours earlier after having stopped and attacked opposition party activists in the same spot late on Sunday night.

Opposition demonstrators regrouped on Monday afternoon and rallied without hindrance in Republic Square but ran quickly into a phalanx of police when they tried to march down a main boulevard, witnesses said.

About 500 police wearing helmets and body armour and brandishing truncheons stood in a multi-tiered cordon across the boulevard close to the Hotel Balkan. The police commander told opposition leader Zoran Djindjic that he would not let them pass but would not resort to force without provocation, a Reuters news team said.
Protest organisers established a 100-metre (330-foot) gap between demonstrators and police. Djindjic indicated that to avoid bloodshed he would try to end the rally and have people disperse.

But it was unclear if appeals to reason would succeed as tension and anger pervaded the crowd with some militants shouting "ustasha, ustasha" at police, a term of abuse normally reserved for Croatian fascists.
